notes: Owned PiCode surface, grounded in the read-only product tree at ~/picode (README, docs/, docs-site/, docs/architecture/) and the public repo. claimed items are eligible for sync into competitors/picode.json.
positioning: Owned reference ADE for supervising real Pi agents from the browser: workspace agent fleets, tmux-backed terminals that outlive the tab, one human inbox, local-first orchestration, and mobile supervision.

agent_support.name: real pi processes as the managed runtime
agent_support.summary: Every agent is a user-installed pi process, launched either as the genuine TUI in tmux or as pi --mode rpc structured chat.

agent_support.name: agent CLI catalog beyond pi
agent_support.summary: Claude Code, Codex, Grok, Hermes Agent, OpenCode, Muse Code, Antigravity and Omp open interactive terminals with activity reporting where the vendor exposes a signal.

agent_support.name: per-agent provider, model and thinking level
agent_support.summary: Stored per agent and passed to pi as --provider/--model/--thinking; pi's own auth.json stays the credential source of truth.

agent_support.name: first-class sub-agent delegation
agent_support.summary: Core has no sub-agent routing; roles and delegation are opt-in pi packages (for example pi-roles), not daemon behaviour.

orchestration.name: agent fleet across workspaces
orchestration.summary: Workspaces own agents (plus free agents outside a workspace), each with its own launch settings and working directory.

orchestration.name: durable task delivery with steer and follow-up
orchestration.summary: A queued task with a prompt waits for the agent to settle; steer and follow_up reach an agent while a turn is still running.

orchestration.name: human inbox for questions, approvals and results
orchestration.summary: Blocking questions and approvals, settled runs and unexpected exits collect in one inbox; TUI-sourced items are delivered inside the terminal.

orchestration.name: inter-agent messaging broker
orchestration.summary: An MCP server (list_contacts, send_message, read_messages, ack_messages) plus a durable peer mailbox lets named agents message each other.

orchestration.name: automations on cron or webhook
orchestration.summary: Per-rule schedules with deterministic jitter, webhook fire endpoint, run accounting, watchdog, cost cap and one catch-up run after an outage.

orchestration.name: canvas board of agent, terminal, note, file and diff panels
orchestration.summary: Named boards on a pan/zoom plane; edges grant a contact, never a transcript.

orchestration.name: own agent approval policy
orchestration.summary: PiCode surfaces the dialogs and permission prompts the runtime reports; an auto-approve policy is explicitly undecided.

workspace_isolation.name: per-agent working directory
workspace_isolation.summary: A workspace registers a folder; an agent may carry its own workPath, and server-created work directories live under the PiCode data dir.

workspace_isolation.name: tmux session per agent and per project shell
workspace_isolation.summary: Closing the browser only detaches; the systemd unit's KillMode=process keeps tmux-owned terminals alive across daemon restarts.

workspace_isolation.name: private per-agent pi session directory
workspace_isolation.summary: Each agent gets its own session bucket in addition to the workspace cwd bucket.

workspace_isolation.name: git worktree visibility and composed worktree actions
workspace_isolation.summary: Reads the worktree graph per git-common-dir and composes create/prune/remove under <root>/.worktrees/<name> instead of acting silently.

workspace_isolation.name: agent sandboxing
workspace_isolation.summary: Explicit non-goal: agents execute with the invoking user's permissions, like pi itself; containers exist only in the shared-box gateway topology.

review_shipping.name: working-tree review with per-agent attribution
review_shipping.summary: Porcelain status re-anchored to the owner cwd with per-file add/del counts, and an inspector rail that narrows to what this agent edited.

review_shipping.name: file browse and edit with previews
review_shipping.summary: Read/write text, blob and file routes, an editor with Save, and sandboxed HTML/markdown previews behind preview tickets.

review_shipping.name: commit DAG, refs and worktrees view
review_shipping.summary: Commit graph with upstream/ahead/behind/gone/merged refs, remotes and worktrees, plus per-file patches read with --first-parent.

review_shipping.name: composed git actions with risk tiers
review_shipping.summary: Git writes are prepared as an exact command with a risk tier; tier C needs a typed phrase, and nothing auto-executes.

review_shipping.name: delivery declarations with integration observation
review_shipping.summary: Agents register revision-bound changes and request review; PiCode observes local refs and receipts and never merges, runs checks or publishes.

review_shipping.name: cross-CLI session handoff
review_shipping.summary: A handoff plan previews, repairs and writes a transcript or a markdown brief into the target CLI's own session store, with lineage recorded.

remote_mobile.name: mobile PWA for supervision
remote_mobile.summary: A four-tab phone app (Now, Inbox, Work, More) that installs from the browser and shares the same server as desktop.

remote_mobile.name: push notifications implemented in-tree
remote_mobile.summary: VAPID keys, per-message encryption and subscription routes in the standard library, fired for blocked agents, blocking inbox items and finished runs.

remote_mobile.name: per-device pairing
remote_mobile.summary: One-use codes with ten-minute expiry and lockout, cookie or bearer sessions, and revocable devices; sessions expire after long idleness.

remote_mobile.name: remote access on a private network
remote_mobile.summary: mkcert or Tailscale certificates with persisted bind and public-URL settings, plus server.json / remote.json discovery.

remote_mobile.name: shared-box gateway
remote_mobile.summary: A root unit maps tailnet identities to Linux users and proxies to per-user daemons, with an optional OIDC listener behind a TLS proxy.

remote_mobile.name: Windows desktop shell
remote_mobile.summary: Tauri 2 + WebView2 shell plus a tray/logon tool; the server itself still runs inside WSL.

context_memory.name: SQLite orchestration overlay
context_memory.summary: ~/.picode/picode.db holds workspaces, agents, terminals, tasks, inbox, messages, events and settings; conversations stay in pi's own session files.

context_memory.name: change feed over SSE
context_memory.summary: Every store mutation appends a typed event row in the same transaction and fans out over SSE, with a reset cursor past the retention window.

context_memory.name: cross-CLI session read and write
context_memory.summary: Watchers read each vendor's session store and writers publish new session artifacts atomically where the vendor allows it.

context_memory.name: per-CLI long-term memory panes
context_memory.summary: Memory tiers are declared per CLI (editable, readonly, none, unknown); unresolved stores report resolved=false and refuse instead of guessing.

context_memory.name: credential vault for provider accounts
context_memory.summary: AES-256-GCM vault under the PiCode data dir holds provider accounts for pi and the guest CLIs; pi's auth.json stays owned by pi.

context_memory.name: backup and restore of PiCode data
context_memory.summary: Snapshots cover the database, pinned artifacts, pi settings and optionally sessions and secrets; restore is an atomic swap and never touches project folders.

integrations.name: MCP servers exposing PiCode tools
integrations.summary: Families include computer, browser, inbox (notify_human, ask_human), checklist and delivery, with identity and daemon discovery from the environment.

integrations.name: per-CLI connector configuration
integrations.summary: One pane writes each vendor's own MCP configuration file, with vendor-truthful scope rules instead of a synthetic shared registry.

integrations.name: signed webhooks
integrations.summary: Durable events become HMAC-SHA256 POSTs with ordered at-least-once retries, a request bound and link-local/metadata addresses refused.

integrations.name: pi packages and installable pi extensions
integrations.summary: A package pane covers pi and the guest CLIs, while in-tree MIT packages (pi-roles, pi-inbox, pi-checklist, pi-compact, pi-diff, pi-browser, pi-computer, pi-delivery, pi-sysadmin, connectors) stay installable.

integrations.name: browser extension to agent handoff
integrations.summary: An MV3 extension sideloads with a native-messaging host and sends page context to an existing agent, with an optional capped act-on-page loop.

integrations.name: local model manager
integrations.summary: An optional llama.cpp manager route runs a local model service alongside the daemon.
